accuracy.evidence: Curriculum wording quoted from the National Curriculum in England Year 4 Living things and their habitats statutory requirement (explore and use classification keys to help group, identify and name a variety of living things in their local and wider environment), with the Year 6 follow-on on classifying by characteristics. The n - 1 questions rule (p1, p3, m2) is the count of internal nodes in a binary branching key with n end points and was checked at the corners of every parameter range. Leg counts (insects 6, spiders 8, woodlouse 14) and the leaf features (holly simple with spines, oak simple and lobed, horse chestnut palmate with 5 to 7 leaflets, ash pinnate) checked against the Natural History Museum and Woodland Trust tree ID pages.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips reported for KS2 keys: calling a spider an insect (step 1 prediction, m3, challenge 'insect' and 'depends'), opinion or vague questions such as cute, pretty or big (step 2 prediction and the five-question judging task, p4, challenge 'opinion' and 'vague'), double-barrelled questions (legs and wings in step 2, m4 and the challenge), questions every member answers the same way so nothing splits (is it alive, is it an animal in steps 3 and 4, m5), and reading a compound leaf as one piece (step 5 prediction, m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagkey is built around a live two-level branching key drawn on the canvas: answering lights the yes or no branch and reveals the named end, and the build step fills an empty key node by node as the child chooses splitting questions. Minibeast and grouping labs (flagbug, flagmbhab and the toy sorter flagsort) sort into bins or hoops; none walks or builds a dichotomous tree. lab_distinct gate passes under 30% against every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child names four minibeasts and four leaves by answering one question at a time and watches the path light up, so the idea of following branches comes from doing it. Choosing 'Is it alive?' for bee, butterfly, fish and frog is rejected with 'every one would say yes, the group does not split', which discovers what a useful question is before the build step asks for three of them in a row. The text after each task only confirms.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong answers that the lab then disproves: 'Yes, spiders are insects' (the key sends the spider down the no branch with 8 legs), 'Yes, anyone can answer it' for 'Is it pretty?' (the judging task rejects opinion questions), and 'Yes' for a five-leaflet leaf being in one piece (the leaf key sends horse chestnut down the no branch).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating challenge questions; every wrong option carries one of 14 messages naming the slip: counting instead of naming, food chain confusion, opinion, vague size, spider as insect, 'depends on the spider', one group or many groups instead of two, a question everyone answers yes to, too short versus two-in-one, and ash or horse chestnut leaflets versus a one-piece prickly holly leaf.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short sentences with one concrete example each (garden minibeast, spider legs, cute versus wings, splitting into yes and no groups) and pass the family kid readability limit; the adult text uses the precise terms classification key, dichotomous key, observable feature and branching diagram and quotes the Year 4 statement. Canvas text is limited to the key questions, yes, no and names.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (what a key is, following a branch, good questions, splitting until each is alone). Items split into counting questions in a key (p1, p3, m2), counting branch members (p2, m1), choosing good questions (p4, m4, m5), applying the key (m3, m6) and purpose (m7); no two items test the same thing the same way.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and iPhone 13 dark screenshots of every step before and after Show me: the root, two second questions and four ends fit with readable two-line labels; Yes and No canvas buttons are about 64 px tall; the split and build steps show three full-width question rows; leaf ends now draw each leaf shape (holly, oak, fan, ash) instead of one repeated emoji, and the animal emoji sits on a white badge so the spider is visible in dark mode.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap has a labelled button twin below (Yes, No, Good question, Not good, each candidate question, Next one). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each answer with the reason and the next question. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors; the extra screenshot pass found no page errors.
